item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 102350
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Punta
Baja, Mexico, and on Hurricane Simon, located less than one hundred
miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to develop south or southwest of
the coast of Mexico by early next week. Environmental conditions are
expected to be conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a
tropical depression is likely to form by the middle or latter half
of next week as the system moves generally west-northwestward at
around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 110243
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Advisory Number  56
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026
 
...RACHEL SHOWING SIGNS OF WEAKENING AS IT TURNS
NORTH-NORTHEASTWARD...
...STRONG WINDS EXPECTED IN PORTIONS OF THE BAJA CALIFORNIA
PENINSULA TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...30.0N 116.5W
ABOUT 40 MI...65 KM W OF PUNTA BAJA MEXICO
ABOUT 190 MI...305 KM S OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 15 DEGREES AT 36 MPH...57 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...987 MB...29.15 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California and Baja California Sur, from Punta
Eugenia northward to the U.S./Mexico Border
* East coast of Baja California, from Isla San Luis northward to
Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Southern California coast from the U.S/Mexico Border northward to
the San Diego/Orange County Line
* East coast of Baja California, from Bahia De Los Angeles
northward to Isla San Luis
* Northwest Mexico from Puerto Libertad to Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area.
 
For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel
was located near latitude 30.0 North, longitude 116.5 West. The
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the north-northeast near 36
mph (57 km/h) and this motion is expected to persist as Rachel moves
onshore over northern Baja California tonight. Rachel is forecast to
dissipate shortly thereafter early Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.
Slow weakening is forecast, and Rachel is expected to dissipate over
the southwestern U.S. on Sunday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 990 mb (29.24 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected to occur over portions
of the Baja California Peninsula within the Tropical Storm Warning
area tonight and continue into Sunday morning. Tropical storm
conditions are also possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area in
extreme Southern California, eastern Baja California, and portions
of northwest Mexico beginning tonight or early Sunday. Strong gusty
winds associated with the system are expected to spread over
interior portions of the Southwest United States, especially in
areas of higher terrain, tonight through early next week.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of
Baja California this weekend.
 
Rachel and its associated moisture will also bring rainfall of 1 to
3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 inches in portions of
the Southwest United States this weekend. This will lead to
increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for significant flash
and urban flooding.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and
the Flash Flood Risk graphic at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Waves generated by Rachel will continue to build along the
coasts of Southern California and northern Baja California this
weekend. These waves, combined with an incoming long-period
southerly swell, will cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Coastal flooding and erosion are expected to worsen
tonight into Sunday morning as the highest waves coincide with the
high tides and water levels that are already running well above
predicted levels. Moderate to major coastal flooding is expected,
with hazardous coastal conditions continuing into early next week.
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 PM PDT.
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Adams

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 56
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 110243
TCDEP3
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Discussion Number  56
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026
 
Rachel has lacked organized deep convection for more than 12 hours,
with much of the forcing associated with the system now driven by a
nearby mid- to upper-level trough rather than tropical processes. In
addition, the low-level circulation has become increasingly
elongated, and the center is no longer well-defined. Given these
structural changes and the lack of organized deep convection, Rachel
is now classified as a post-tropical cyclone. Based on these data,
and a previous ASCAT-B scatterometer pass earlier today, the initial
intensity was lowered to 50 kt.
 
The initial motion is estimated to be north-northeastward, or 015/31
kt, and the system is expected to accelerate as it moves inland. The
updated NHC track forecast was nudged eastward a bit, but otherwise
closely mirrors the previous forecast and aligns well with the
latest HCCA and GDMI consensus aids.
 
Rachel is now a post-tropical cyclone, but that does not mean the
threat has diminished. Watches and warnings remain unchanged for
Mexico and Southern California, since expected impacts from the
system remain the same and the remnants of Rachel will continue to
produce heavy rainfall and gusty winds. See products issued by the
Weather Prediction Center and local National Weather Service offices
for more information.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to make landfall along the coast of northern
Baja California later tonight. Tropical storm conditions are
expected in portions of northern Baja California and portions of
northwestern Mexico, where Tropical Storm Warnings are in effect.
Tropical storm conditions are also possible in extreme Southern
California, eastern Baja California, and portions of northwestern
Mexico where Tropical Storm Watches are in effect.
 
2. Damaging wind gusts associated with Rachel and its remnants are
expected to spread over portions of northwestern Mexico and interior
portions of the Southwest United States, especially in areas of
higher terrain, tonight and Sunday.
 
3. Rachel and its moisture will continue to spread over portions of
the Southwest United States and northern Baja California peninsula.
This will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and for the
potential for significant flash and urban flooding this weekend.
 
4. Waves generated by Rachel, combined with an incoming long-period
southerly swell, will produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along the coasts of Southern California and northern Baja
California. Major coastal flooding has already been occurring in
some areas, with observed water levels running as much as 1.5 feet
above predictions. Coastal flooding and erosion are expected to
worsen tonight into Sunday morning as the highest waves associated
with Rachel coincide with high tides and already elevated water
levels. Hazardous coastal conditions are expected to continue into
early next week. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  11/0300Z 30.0N 116.5W   50 KT  60 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
 12H  11/1200Z 34.5N 114.9W   45 KT  50 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
 24H  12/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Adams

ABOUT 165 MI...260 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...155 MPH...250 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...928 MB...27.41 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued 36
hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area beginning tonight.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM CST (0300 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 18.2 North, longitude 104.8 West. Simon is moving
toward the north near 5 mph (7 km/h) and this general motion is
expected to continue over the next day or two. On the forecast
track, Simon is expected to be near or just inland over west-central
Mexico on Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 155 mph (250 km/h)
with higher gusts. Simon is a category 4 hurricane on the
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity are
anticipated, but Simon is still forecast to approach the coast of
west-central Mexico as a major hurricane on Sunday. Rapid weakening
could occur if the core of Simon moves fully onshore.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles
(150 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 928 mb (27.41 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the southern part of the
Hurricane Warning area beginning early Sunday, with tropical storm
conditions expected as soon as later tonight with these winds
spreading northward thereafter. Tropical storm conditions are
possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area beginning tonight.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 10 to 20
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals of 30 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima,
and Jalisco through Sunday. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the immediate
coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall. Near
the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and destructive
waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1200 AM CST.
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 110233
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 PM CST Sat Oct 10 2026
 
The compact core of very dangerous Hurricane Simon is inching toward
west-central Mexico. The northern eyewall is only about 30 n mi off
the coast, and conditions are expected to quickly deteriorate later
tonight. The major hurricane appears to be getting stronger and has
a distinct and small eye, surrounded by symmetric and intense deep
convection. The initial intensity is nudged up to 135 kt, near the
upper end of the latest satellite estimates. The Air Force Hurricane
Hunters are scheduled to investigate the system in a few hours, and
the data they collect will be very helpful to better assess Simon's
intensity and structure.
 
Simon has been crawling northward, with the latest initial motion
estimated to be 360/4 kt. A slightly faster northward or
north-northwestward motion is expected later tonight, and the major
hurricane will either make landfall or skirt the coast of
west-central Mexico on Sunday. The models remain inconsistent in
showing whether landfall will occur or not. Regardless, significant
or catastrophic wind, surge, and rainfall appears likely over
portions of west-central Mexico later tonight and Sunday.
 
Fluctuations in strength are expected until the core of Simon
reaches the coast. Rapid weakening is forecast once the system
interacts with land, and it could weaken at a much faster pace if it
moves to the east of the official track. Due to the complexity of
how much land Simon will interacts with, the intensity forecast is
of low confidence.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a
Hurricane Warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to El Roblito.
Preparations to protect life and property should be rushed to
completion.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico over the next few days. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
